transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (ZenHealth IT Security), Tomás Ruiz (ZenHealth Platform Eng), Asha Patel (ZenHealth Identity Admin)
Recording: internal-fireflies-link/ff-20250311-zen

Summary: brief review of SAML SSO setup, SCIM provisioning options, and RBAC/least-privilege recommendations. Main customer ask: ensure automatic user provisioning with group-to-role mapping, certificate rotation process, audit log retention and export for SOC 2, and minimal privileged service accounts.

Topics covered: SAML metadata, IdP (Okta) configuration, SCIM user sync, attribute mapping (email, displayName, groups), just-in-time (JIT) vs SCIM provisioning, RBAC role model, service principal least-privilege, audit logs retention and export, encryption at rest/KMS notes.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump in. Marcus is here for the deep technical bits.
[00:09] Priya Nair: Hi Lena, thanks. Priya here, and Tomás and Asha are on.
[00:12] Tomás Ruiz: Yep, Tomás. Sorry for the delay, had an exec thing.
[00:16] Asha Patel: Asha here.
[00:19] Lena Park: Awesome. Marcus, want to kick off with high level?
[00:22] Marcus Li: Sure. Quick agenda: one, confirm your IdP — you mentioned Okta in the notes — two, SCIM vs JIT provisioning and recommended flow, three, RBAC mapping examples for least privilege, and four, audit log and cert rotation process. We'll leave 15 minutes for Q&A and next steps.
[00:40] Asha Patel: Correct, Okta. We're mostly on Okta enterprise org. We also have a couple teams on Azure AD but Okta will be primary for the pilot.
[00:48] Marcus Li: Good. For Okta we provide a SAML 2.0 app template and a SCIM connector. You can do either or both: SAML handles auth and SSO, SCIM does provisioning. We often recommend SAML + SCIM for enterprise so you get SSO and automated user lifecycle.
[01:05] Tomás Ruiz: We're sensitive to SCIM updating users — we need strict controls on which attributes can be provisioned and who can trigger deletions.
[01:12] Marcus Li: Absolutely. Our SCIM endpoint accepts standard v2 requests. You can scope provisioning to specific Okta groups; we support group-based scoping so only users in mapped groups get created. Deprovisioning can be configured as either disable or delete. For SOC 2 teams we usually recommend disable first and then a retention policy.
[01:33] Priya Nair: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs for user lifecycle events and SSO events for at least one year for our internal control evidence.
[01:41] Marcus Li: Redwood stores audit events in the control plane and ships them to customer-configured sinks for Dedicated or Private customers. For Hosted customers we can provide export via S3 push or syslog. Retention windows are configurable; default hosted retention is 90 days but for SOC 2 we can enable 12-month retention and a long-term export. We'll follow up with the export format.
[02:03] Asha Patel: Is the export tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody.
[02:08] Marcus Li: The exported logs are written to the customer's S3 bucket (or external syslog) with server-side encryption; you can enable object lock and versioning on your bucket to ensure immutability. For Private deployments you can send logs to your internal SIEM. We also sign exported files using a rotating key so you can verify integrity.
[02:29] Tomás Ruiz: That signing is great. Can you share the signing algorithm and rotation cadence?
[02:33] Marcus Li: Currently we use SHA256-based HMAC with a key rotated every 30 days by default; we can adjust cadence. For exports we include a manifest file with SHA256 checksums and a signed header.
[02:46] Priya Nair: Ok. Now SAML metadata: Asha will be configuring Okta. What exactly do we need from Redwood?
[02:52] Lena Park: We will provide the SAML metadata XML, ACS URL, entityID, and the public cert for signing assertions if you choose to validate. Also steps for automated cert rotation.
[03:04] Asha Patel: Cert rotation — who rotates first? If Redwood rotates first and Okta caches the old cert, will users break?
[03:11] Marcus Li: Good question. We support a dual-cert window to avoid outages: we publish the new cert to our metadata and keep the old cert valid for X hours; Okta typically polls metadata or you can upload metadata manually. We recommend configuring Okta to accept both certs during rotation window. We'll include a step-by-step checklist.
[03:30] Tomás Ruiz: Is there an API to trigger certificate rotation manually? Some of our automation might want to call it.
[03:36] Marcus Li: Yes, for Dedicated/Private there's an admin API to rotate signing certs. For Hosted customers we can do it via support request but are rolling out self-service rotation in the console. We'll mark that in the action items.
[03:47] Priya Nair: On SCIM attributes: we want email, name, employeeId, manager, and groups. But for manager and employeeId we have some internal format. How flexible is the mapping?
[03:57] Marcus Li: SCIM attribute mapping is configurable. Our connector maps common attributes out-of-the-box; you can remap attributes in Okta or in Redwood's mapping UI. For employeeId we support any string attribute; for manager we accept manager as a reference to another SCIM user or a managerEmail attribute depending on your Okta config. We'll share examples.
[04:18] Asha Patel: For groups, can we map Okta groups to Redwood roles? Example: Okta group 'zen-admins' => Redwood role 'org-admin' with elevated privileges, but that should exclude access to billing APIs.
[04:29] Marcus Li: Yes, group-to-role mapping is first-class. You can create multiple role mappings: e.g., zen-admins -> org-admin (no billing), zen-platform -> workspace-admin, zen-readonly -> viewer. We recommend separating billing access into a different role and not mapping any Okta group to billing by default. Billing access is managed via a separate billing seat and support workflow for additional approvals.
[04:51] Tomás Ruiz: We have a regulatory need for least privilege and periodic access reviews. How does Redwood support access certification?
[04:59] Marcus Li: We provide audit logs for role changes and user membership. For Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your GRC tooling; we can export membership snapshots on a schedule (CSV) for attestations. We're also experimenting with built-in access review flows in the console — currently beta. We'll include the workarounds: scheduled exports and webhook notifications on group changes.
[05:20] Priya Nair: About service accounts — we want a service account for automation that can only call the embeddings APIs and not generate completions. Is that feasible?
[05:28] Marcus Li: Yes. Tokens are scoped by route-level permissions in the platform. You can create service tokens with granular scopes: embeddings.read, embeddings.write, completions.create, models.list, etc. For your case create a token with embeddings.* only. Also you can bind tokens to IP allowlists and short TTLs.
[05:44] Asha Patel: Do tokens show up in audit trails? We need to be able to link a token action to a service account and to an owner.
[05:51] Marcus Li: Tokens are logged with token id, associated user or service principal, IP, and action. We also support token metadata fields so you can annotate owner and purpose. Those metadata fields are included in the audit export.
[06:06] Lena Park: Quick interjection — Priya, you mentioned SOC 2 earlier. Are there any controls beyond retention and immutability we should call out?
[06:13] Priya Nair: Encryption key management: we need CMKs, key rotation policy, and separation of duties. Also RBAC hierarchy that prevents a single admin from both assigning roles and approving billing changes.
[06:24] Marcus Li: For encryption at rest we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via cloud KMS integrations, and we log key usage. Key rotation is supported; Redwood does not have plaintext access to customer keys.
[06:42] Tomás Ruiz: For BYOK, is there a requirement on key type or algorithm?
[06:46] Marcus Li: We recommend AES-256 for data keys; the KMS provider handles the master key. For signing we use RSA2048 or RSA3072 for SAML certs but we'll supply specifics in the doc.
[06:58] Asha Patel: On RBAC: can you show an example role matrix? We want minimum privileges for a Platform Engineer vs an App Developer.
[07:05] Marcus Li: Sure — RDW-Role examples: workspace-developer: create/run jobs, view logs for their workspace; no org-level access. workspace-operator: manage deployments in a workspace, can scale instances. org-admin: manage users and roles but we recommend a separate billing-admin role that has only billing.read and billing.update with an approval hook. We'll share a CSV with these mappings and sample Okta group names.
[07:36] Priya Nair: For least-privilege enforcement, are there any guardrails? For example preventing org-admin from granting themselves billing-admin?
[07:44] Marcus Li: By default RBAC is additive; org-admin can manage roles. For stronger separation, you can configure approval workflows in the console where role changes require a second approver. In Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your internal approval system via webhook. We also support time-limited elevations (just-in-time elevation) for sensitive roles.
[08:06] Tomás Ruiz: JIT elevation — is that based on OAuth scopes or temporary role token?
[08:11] Marcus Li: Temporary role tokens. You request elevation and we issue a short-lived token that adds the elevated role claims for a TTL. That request can require MFA and an auditable workflow.
[08:23] Asha Patel: For Okta group sync, if someone moves between groups quickly, how does Redwood reconcile race conditions? We've had issues where group membership lags.
[08:33] Marcus Li: Our SCIM connector applies atomic operations where possible and uses a last-writer-wins model based on timestamps. There's also a reconciliation job that runs every X minutes to reconcile differences. For critical flows you can hook into webhooks to get immediate notifications on group changes. We'll document common troubleshooting steps.
[08:55] Lena Park: Switching gears — attack surface: what are the recommended least-privilege network controls?
[09:00] Marcus Li: We advise IP allowlisting for admin endpoints, restricted egress rules for private deployments, and VPC peering for Dedicated. Console admin actions should be limited to specific subnets or via bastion. Also enable SSO with MFA for all org-admins.
[09:15] Priya Nair: Does Redwood support SAML attribute-based access control (ABAC) or only group-based RBAC?
[09:21] Marcus Li: Primarily group-based RBAC, but you can use attributes in the SCIM mapping and our rule engine to derive roles from attributes. For example, department=security + contractType=fulltime => security-reader. It's not a full ABAC engine but can express common patterns.
[09:41] Tomás Ruiz: About logs again — can we get real-time streaming into Splunk?
[09:46] Marcus Li: Yes. We have a Splunk HEC (HTTP Event Collector) integration. For high-throughput we recommend batching and compressing events; we can provide a connector config and a best-practices doc.
[09:58] Asha Patel: Any PII in logs? We must ensure PHI isn't in the auth logs for compliance reasons.
[10:05] Marcus Li: We redact user content from request payloads in logs by default. Auth logs include identifiers (user id, email) but no content. For PHI-sensitive customers we can further obfuscate email and use pseudonymous ids. We'll note that in the doc.
[10:21] Priya Nair: What about SCIM deprovisioning hooks — can we call our HR system to validate termination before Redwood deletes accounts?
[10:29] Marcus Li: You can plug a webhook that fires on deprovision events. The webhook can return a hold signal; Redwood will then convert delete to disable if the webhook indicates a pending HR process. That said, for immediate compliance terminations you can bypass hooks with a manual admin operation.
[10:45] Tomás Ruiz: On rotation of service account keys, what is the TTL recommended? We prefer short lived.
[10:50] Marcus Li: For service tokens, we recommend rotating every 7 days or less for high-risk roles; shorter TTLs (minutes/hours) for ephemeral tasks. We also support automatic rotation and CA-signed ephemeral token flows via workload identity.
[11:05] Asha Patel: Ok, let's surface a couple of edge cases: 1) If a user is in two Okta groups mapped to different Redwood roles, which wins? 2) If SCIM update fails midway, do you leave partial state?
[11:15] Marcus Li: For 1, we evaluate the highest privilege role (role precedence). We include precedence rules in the mapping UI so you can control which role wins. For 2, we try to apply operations idempotently; if a multi-step update fails we have a reconciliation job and a retry queue. Partial state is possible in rare cases; we surface failures in the audit log and a reconciliation task is queued.
[11:37] Priya Nair: Good to know. For SOC 2 evidence, will Redwood provide a mapping of controls to logs and screenshots for us?
[11:44] Lena Park: Yes, we prepare a controls mapping for SOC 2 customers with sample evidence — log exports, role change audit screenshots, and our SOC 2 report references. We'll share that as a follow-up.
[11:55] Tomás Ruiz: A few quick technical follow-ups: 1) sample SCIM payloads, 2) rollback strategy for mass deprovision, 3) how to test cert rotation on a staging org.
[12:06] Marcus Li: We'll include sample payloads and a staging checklist. For rollback we recommend disable-first, then staged deletes with a dry-run mode — we have a dry-run API for SCIM so you can see the changes without applying them. For cert rotation testing, use a staging metadata feed and validate assertions with our test endpoint.
[12:25] Asha Patel: Great. One more — can we lock down console UI so only certain IP ranges can access billing pages?
[12:31] Marcus Li: Yes, IP restrictions can be applied per-role for console access in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have org-wide IP allowlist for admin console. Billing role specific restrictions are in our roadmap but we can implement via a custom proxy for high-reg customers.
[12:46] Priya Nair: Ok that's very helpful.
[12:50] Lena Park: Let's do a short recap and next steps.
[12:54] Lena Park: Action items: Marcus will send RBAC CSV and SCIM examples; I'll send SAML metadata and the cert rotation checklist; Asha will share Okta groups and mapping details. Customer to review and confirm by next Tuesday.
[13:08] Tomás Ruiz: Sounds good.
[13:10] Asha Patel: I'll get the groups list to you by Monday.
[13:12] Priya Nair: We'll prioritize the SOC 2 evidence mapping after we see the RBAC matrix.
[13:16] Marcus Li: I'll also include sample Splunk config and HEC tokens example.
[13:20] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll email the follow-ups and set up any follow-up technical workshop if needed.
[13:27] Priya Nair: Thank you.
[13:29] Meeting ended.
